html:
The Revival Process was a campaign by the communist government of Todor Zhivkov from 1984 to 1989 to force the Turks and other Muslims of Bulgaria to take Bulgarian names and give up their language and customs.

Troops surrounded villages, and people were made to accept new names on their papers. Speaking Turkish in public and wearing traditional dress were banned, and protesters were killed. In May 1989 protests broke out, and the regime then forced people out, so that about 360,000 Turks crossed into Turkey that summer in what was called the Great Excursion. Many later returned. The campaign helped bring down Zhivkov in November 1989 during the revolutions of 1989, and the ban on names was lifted. It shaped the politics of Bulgaria and its ties with Turkey.
sum: The Revival Process was a campaign by the communist government of Todor Zhivkov from 1984 to 1989 to force the Turks and other Muslims of Bulgaria to take Bulgarian names and give up their language and customs.
